reference_use.conclusion: The snapshot (project b4d606d, Mathlib 25730c7c) has the same Ch07 contract as the workspace and contains no proof to reuse for this node: no cmcdt_lpi_pc name and no Lipschitz-piece integrality lemma (no match). No accepted DAG theorem has any of the six child statements; the one same-shape bi-Lipschitz partition is an unaccepted node under another parent, so fresh names are used. Mathlib provides every tool the children use: the approximately-linear partition, antilipschitz constants of injective maps, openness of linear independence, Lusin–Souslin images and measurable embeddings, measurability of fderiv and of the differentiability set, Rademacher, the derivative bound for Lipschitz maps, vanishing of alternating maps on dependent families, countable additivity of set integrals and lintegrals, and the opnorm bound for alternating maps. SimonGMT provides rectifiability of Lipschitz ranges, test forms and mass as a supremum over admissible forms. MultiVector P n has no automatic second-countability instance, so strong measurability of the orientation field is proved through the finite coordinate expansion of α ↦ α(z), which was checked in Lean. All six child types elaborate. Three children are proved outright at their frozen types, the other three are derived from their siblings and the selected node's resolved prerequisites, and the selected frozen type is derived from the children; every check reports axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

rationale:
Split into six new depth-6 leaves. The selected node keeps only step 8 of its supplied proof (summation of the pieces), and its Lean assembly from three of the children compiles.

Why split. The supplied proof (steps 1–8) chains five independent techniques. Steps 1–2 reduce to the regular set A⁺ using Rademacher's theorem and alternation. Step 3 is Mathlib's approximately-linear partition. Step 5 uses Lusin–Souslin. Steps 4–5 build the induced orientation with a.e. tangent planes. Steps 5–7 construct one piece current through int_density_imrep, (IMC)(b) and the area formulas, with its mass bound. Each child is a classical, reusable statement: the regular-part reduction of a pulled-back integrand, a bi-Lipschitz partition, a Lusin–Souslin inverse, the push-forward density g∘H⁻¹, the induced orientation J⁻¹·DH_#e (Simon 6.3.5, 3.7), and H_#(g[[B]]) being integer multiplicity on one bi-Lipschitz piece (Simon 6.3.6–3.9). As a single Lean proof this is roughly 600 lines. The integrality decomposition expected this node to split once more into depth-6 leaves, so every child below is a leaf, and each was checked to be provable as stated (see Checks).

Children (keys → Lean names; all prefixed cmcdt_lpi_pc_, a prefix used nowhere else):
- regular_reduction → cmcdt_lpi_pc_regular_part_reduction (steps 1–2). A⁺ := {u ∈ A : DifferentiableAt, DH injective, g ≠ 0} is Borel; Ψ_ω is integrable on A; and ∫_A Ψ_ω = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω. No dependencies.
- bilip_partition → cmcdt_lpi_pc_bilipschitz_partition (step 3). A Borel set on which DH exists and is injective splits into disjoint Borel pieces C_l with κ_l|a − a'| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| on each piece. No dependencies.
- measurable_inverse → cmcdt_lpi_pc_measurable_inverse (step 5, bullets 1–2). If H is continuous and injective on a Borel set B, then H(B) is Borel and H has a Borel left inverse h on B. No dependencies.
- piece_multiplicity → cmcdt_lpi_pc_piece_multiplicity (step 5 density, with step 4's bound J ≤ Lⁿ). m := 1_{H(B)}·g∘h is measurable and integer-valued with m∘H = g on B, Hⁿ(H(B)) < ∞, and ∫_{H(B)}|m| dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫_B|g|. Depends on measurable_inverse. Cites the Gram area formula (lintegral form) and span_orientation.
- piece_orientation → cmcdt_lpi_pc_piece_orientation (steps 4–5). η := 1_{H(B)}·(J⁻¹ev_v)∘h is strongly measurable and a unit orientation of range DH(u) at H(u), with J·η(H u)(α) = α(DH(u)e), and it orients the approximate tangent planes of H(B) Hⁿ-a.e. Depends on measurable_inverse. Cites piece_tangent, span_orientation and the Gram area formula (lintegral form).
- single_piece_current → cmcdt_lpi_pc_piece_current (steps 5–7). Under the antecedents (L3) and (IMC)(b), each bi-Lipschitz piece with nonzero integrable integer weight gives an integer multiplicity Φ with M(Φ) ≤ Lⁿ∫_B|g| and Φ(ω) = ∫_B g·ω(H)(DH e). Depends on measurable_inverse, piece_multiplicity and piece_orientation. Cites int_density_imrep and the Gram area formula (Bochner form).

How the children give the selected statement (supplied step 8, with only the children's conclusions as input). Fix CB, IMC, IMSc and N', k, L, H, A, g as in the selected type, and let n = k + 1.
1. regular_reduction (P := N') gives: A⁺ is Borel; for every test form ω, Ψ_ω is integrable on A and ∫_A Ψ_ω = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω.
2. bilip_partition with B := A⁺ (DH exists and is injective on A⁺ by definition) gives disjoint Borel C_l with ⋃_l C_l = A⁺ and constants κ_l.
3. For each l, apply single_piece_current with (L3) := CB.2.2, (IMC)(b) := IMC.2.1, B := C_l and κ := κ_l. Because C_l ⊆ A⁺ ⊆ A, H is differentiable with injective derivative on C_l, g ≠ 0 on C_l, and g is integrable on C_l. This gives integer multiplicity Φ_l with M(Φ_l) ≤ Lⁿ∫⁻_{C_l}|g| and Φ_l(ω) = ∫_{C_l} Ψ_ω.
4. Σ_l M(Φ_l) ≤ Lⁿ Σ_l ∫⁻_{C_l}|g| = Lⁿ∫⁻_{A⁺}|g| ≤ Lⁿ∫⁻_A|g| < ∞, by ENNReal.tsum_mul_left, lintegral_iUnion and the integrability of g on A.
5. IMSc (P := N', this k) gives S with HasSum (Φ_l(ω)) (S(ω)), and S is integer multiplicity because every Φ_l is.
6. hasSum_integral_iUnion gives HasSum (∫_{C_l} Ψ_ω) (∫_{⋃C_l} Ψ_ω). By uniqueness of sums, S(ω) = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω = ∫_A Ψ_ω, which is the required formula.
This assembly compiles against the exact selected frozen type (assembly_check).

Antecedent and prerequisite design. The selected type passes CB, IMC and IMSc as antecedents. single_piece_current receives only (L3) and (IMC)(b), copied verbatim from the conjuncts CB.2.2 and IMC.2.1. As a result no child waits on the unaccepted covector-bounds theorem, whose name appears in no child proof. The selected node's five resolved prerequisites reach a child through the controller's inheritance rule only when that child's frozen proof text names them; inherited.py was checked for this. Each child names exactly the ones it uses, and the shared reference_use text names none of them. Running the controller's own `cited` function on the rendered texts confirms the inheritance:
- regular_reduction, bilip_partition, measurable_inverse: nothing;
- piece_multiplicity: area_lintegral, span_orientation;
- piece_orientation: piece_tangent, area_lintegral, span_orientation;
- single_piece_current: int_density_imrep, area_integral.
So the first three leaves can start immediately. The other three wait only for prerequisites the selected node already depends on; of these, only span_orientation is unaccepted.

Faithfulness and deviations. Every child follows the corresponding supplied step. These details are filled in where the supplied proof is terse:
- Borel measurability of A⁺ is checked through openness of linear independence instead of the Gram determinant (regular_reduction step 2).
- Borel measurability of Ψ_ω and strong measurability of η use the finite coordinate expansion α(z) = Σ_f ∏_a z_{a,f(a)} α(e'∘f). This implements the supplied "evaluation is continuous" and "Borel into a finite-dimensional space" remarks; Lean synthesizes no second-countability instance for MultiVector P n (regular_reduction step 3, piece_orientation step 3).
- The Borel inverse h is made global by extending it with a constant (measurable_inverse).
The supplied a.e. argument (Rademacher) is kept for step 2. The supplied finiteness argument Hⁿ(N) ≤ Lⁿλ(B) < ∞ is kept in piece_multiplicity step 5, with λ(B) ≤ ∫_B|g| because g ≠ 0 on each piece. No other deviations.

subproblems.title: Regular part of a Lipschitz parametrization: A⁺ is Borel, the pulled-back integrand is integrable and vanishes off A⁺ (supplied steps 1–2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0, let H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith L H), let A ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel, and let g : ℝⁿ → ℤ be measurable with g Lebesgue integrable on A (IntegrableOn (fun u => (g u : ℝ)) A). Write DH(u) := fderiv ℝ H u (the zero map where H is not differentiable), e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a ∈ Fin n) and A⁺ := {u ∈ A : H is differentiable at u, DH(u) is injective and g(u) ≠ 0}. Then A⁺ is Borel, and for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (ω : TestFormOn univ n) the function Ψ_ω(u) := g(u)·ω(H(u))(DH(u)e_0, …, DH(u)e_{n−1}) is Lebesgue integrable on A and ∫_A Ψ_ω dλ = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω dλ (λ = Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (H : Euclid n → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (g : Euclid n → ℤ), LipschitzWith L H → MeasurableSet A → Measurable g → IntegrableOn (fun u => (g u : ℝ)) A → MeasurableSet {u | u ∈ A ∧ DifferentiableAt ℝ H u ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ H u) ∧ g u ≠ 0} ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IntegrableOn (fun u => (g u : ℝ) * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (H u) (fun a => fderiv ℝ H u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))) A ∧ ∫ u in A, (g u : ℝ) * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (H u) (fun a => fderiv ℝ H u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1)) = ∫ u in {u | u ∈ A ∧ DifferentiableAt ℝ H u ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ H u) ∧ g u ≠ 0}, (g u : ℝ) * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (H u) (fun a => fderiv ℝ H u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 2 of the supplied proof of cmcdt_lpi_lipschitz_piece_im (integrability of Ψ_ω; the integrand lives on A⁺), with the omitted details filled in.

Notation: λ is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝⁿ; e'_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin P) is the standard basis of ℝ^P; v(u) := (DH(u)e_a)_{a ∈ Fin n}. A test form ω is C^∞ (hence continuous) as a map ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) and has compact support (IsTestForm).

1. (Injectivity criterion.) For a continuous linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, T is injective iff the family (Te_a)_{a ∈ Fin n} is linearly independent. If T is injective, (Te_a) is the image of the basis (e_a) under a linear map with zero kernel, hence linearly independent (LinearIndependent.map'). Conversely, if (Te_a) is linearly independent and Tw = 0, write w = Σ_a w_a e_a; then Σ_a w_a Te_a = 0, so every w_a = 0 and w = 0 (Mathlib LinearMap.injective_of_linearIndependent, using that the e_a span ℝⁿ).
2. (A⁺ is Borel.) A⁺ = A ∩ D ∩ I ∩ g⁻¹(ℤ ∖ {0}) with D := {u : H is differentiable at u} and I := {u : DH(u) is injective}. D is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt). The set O of injective continuous linear maps ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is open: by step 1 it is the preimage of the open set of linearly independent n-families in (ℝ^P)ⁿ (isOpen_setOfPred_linearIndependent) under the continuous map T ↦ (Te_a)_a. Since u ↦ DH(u) is Borel (measurable_fderiv) and O is open, I = DH⁻¹(O) is Borel. g⁻¹(ℤ ∖ {0}) is measurable because g is. Hence A⁺ is Borel. (This is the Borel condition named in the supplied proof; it is verified here through openness of injectivity rather than through the Gram determinant.)
3. (Ψ_ω is Borel.) The supplied proof obtains this from the Borel measurability of u ↦ DH(u) and the continuity of evaluation; concretely: for z ∈ (ℝ^P)ⁿ write z_{a,i} for the i-th coordinate of z_a, so z_a = Σ_i z_{a,i} e'_i. Multilinearity gives, for every n-covector β on ℝ^P, β(z) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (∏_a z_{a,f(a)})·β(e'_{f(0)}, …, e'_{f(n−1)}). Apply it with β := ω(H(u)) and z := v(u). Each coefficient u ↦ ∏_a (f(a)-th coordinate of DH(u)e_a) is Borel (u ↦ DH(u)e_a is Borel by measurable_fderiv_apply_const, and coordinates are continuous linear), and u ↦ ω(H(u))(e'_{f(0)}, …, e'_{f(n−1)}) is continuous (ω and H are continuous, and evaluation at a fixed tuple is a continuous linear functional on covectors). So u ↦ ω(H(u))(v(u)) is a finite sum of Borel functions, and Ψ_ω = g·ω(H(·))(v(·)) is Borel.
4. (Bound and integrability.) ω is continuous with compact support, so C_ω := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (operator norm; HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). For every u, ‖DH(u)‖ ≤ L (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; this also holds where H is not differentiable, DH(u) being 0 there), so |DH(u)e_a| ≤ ‖DH(u)‖·|e_a| ≤ L. By the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), |ω(H(u))(v(u))| ≤ ‖ω(H(u))‖·∏_a |DH(u)e_a| ≤ C_ω·Lⁿ. Hence |Ψ_ω(u)| ≤ C_ω·Lⁿ·|g(u)| for every u. The right-hand side is integrable on A because g is, and Ψ_ω is measurable by step 3, so Ψ_ω is integrable on A (Integrable.mono').
5. (Ψ_ω vanishes a.e. on A ∖ A⁺.) By Rademacher's theorem (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), H is differentiable at λ-a.e. u ∈ ℝⁿ. Let u ∈ A ∖ A⁺ be such a point. Since u ∈ A and H is differentiable at u, u ∉ A⁺ means that g(u) = 0 or DH(u) is not injective. If g(u) = 0, then Ψ_ω(u) = 0. Otherwise v(u) is linearly dependent by step 1, and an alternating map vanishes on a linearly dependent family (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent applied to ω(H(u))), so ω(H(u))(v(u)) = 0 and Ψ_ω(u) = 0.
6. (Conclusion.) A is measurable, A⁺ ⊆ A, and by step 5, for λ-a.e. u, u ∈ A ∖ A⁺ implies Ψ_ω(u) = 0. Hence ∫_A Ψ_ω dλ = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω dλ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero). Together with steps 2 and 4 this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: T is injective iff (Te_a)_a is linearly independent; hence {u : DH(u) injective} is the Borel preimage of an open set under u ↦ DH(u), and A⁺ is Borel.
The coordinate expansion β(z) = Σ_f (∏_a z_{a,f(a)}) β(e'∘f) shows that Ψ_ω is Borel.
‖ω‖ ≤ C_ω, ‖DH‖ ≤ L and the operator-norm bound give |Ψ_ω| ≤ C_ω Lⁿ |g|, so Ψ_ω is integrable on A.
Rademacher and the vanishing of alternating maps on dependent families give Ψ_ω = 0 a.e. on A ∖ A⁺, hence ∫_A Ψ_ω = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω.

subproblems.title: Countable bi-Lipschitz partition of a Borel set on which the derivative is injective (supplied step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, and let B ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel such that H is differentiable at every a ∈ B with injective derivative DH(a) = fderiv ℝ H a. Then there are Borel sets C_l ⊆ ℝⁿ (l ∈ ℕ), pairwise disjoint, with ⋃_l C_l = B, and constants κ_l > 0 such that κ_l·|a − a'| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| for every l and all a, a' ∈ C_l.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (H : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)), MeasurableSet B → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ H a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ H a)) → ∃ (C : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (κ : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ l, MeasurableSet (C l)) ∧ Pairwise (fun l l' => Disjoint (C l) (C l')) ∧ (⋃ l, C l) = B ∧ (∀ l, 0 < κ l) ∧ ∀ l, ∀ a ∈ C l, ∀ a' ∈ C l, κ l * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖H a - H a'‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the supplied proof of cmcdt_lpi_lipschitz_piece_im (bi-Lipschitz partition), applied to the set s := B.

1. (Coercivity constants.) Let T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be continuous linear. If T is injective, then, ℝⁿ being finite-dimensional and ker T = 0, there is K_T > 0 such that T is K_T-antilipschitz, i.e. |w| ≤ K_T·|Tw| for every w (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith); put κ_T := 1/K_T > 0, so |Tw| ≥ κ_T|w|, and r(T) := κ_T/2. If T is not injective, put κ_T := 1 and r(T) := 1. Thus r(T) > 0 for every T; as a function into ℝ≥0 it satisfies r(T) ≠ 0.
2. (Approximately linear partition.) At every x ∈ B, H is differentiable, so HasFDerivWithinAt H (DH(x)) B x. Mathlib's exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (f := H, s := B, f' := DH, the function r of step 1; ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional and ℝ^P second countable) gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_l ⊆ ℝⁿ (l ∈ ℕ) with B ⊆ ⋃_l t_l and continuous linear maps T_l such that |H(a) − H(a') − T_l(a − a')| ≤ r(T_l)·|a − a'| for all a, a' ∈ B ∩ t_l (ApproximatesLinearOn), and, if B ≠ ∅, T_l = DH(y_l) for some y_l ∈ B, for every l.
3. (Pieces.) Put C_l := B ∩ t_l and κ_l := κ_{T_l}/2 > 0. Each C_l is Borel (B and t_l are), the C_l are pairwise disjoint (the t_l are), and ⋃_l C_l = B ∩ ⋃_l t_l = B.
4. (Lower Lipschitz bound.) Let a, a' ∈ C_l. Then B ≠ ∅, so T_l = DH(y_l) with y_l ∈ B, which is injective by hypothesis; hence |T_l w| ≥ κ_{T_l}|w| for all w and r(T_l) = κ_{T_l}/2. By the triangle inequality and step 2, |H(a) − H(a')| ≥ |T_l(a − a')| − |H(a) − H(a') − T_l(a − a')| ≥ κ_{T_l}|a − a'| − (κ_{T_l}/2)|a − a'| = κ_l·|a − a'|. ∎
proof_key_steps: For injective T choose κ_T > 0 with |Tw| ≥ κ_T|w| (antilipschitz constant of an injective map on a finite-dimensional space) and set r(T) := κ_T/2; set r(T) := 1 otherwise.

Mathlib's exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt for H on B gives disjoint Borel t_l covering B and T_l with H − T_l r(T_l)-Lipschitz on B ∩ t_l, where T_l = DH(y_l), y_l ∈ B, is injective when B ≠ ∅.
C_l := B ∩ t_l are disjoint Borel sets with union B, and the triangle inequality gives |H(a) − H(a')| ≥ (κ_{T_l}/2)|a − a'| on C_l.

subproblems.title: Lusin–Souslin: Borel image and Borel left inverse of a map that is continuous and injective on a Borel set (supplied step 5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, and let B ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel such that H is continuous on B (ContinuousOn H B) and injective on B (InjOn H B). Then H(B) is Borel, and there is a Borel measurable map h : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ with h(H(u)) = u for every u ∈ B.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (H : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)), ContinuousOn H B → MeasurableSet B → InjOn H B → MeasurableSet (H '' B) ∧ ∃ h : Euclid P → Euclid n, Measurable h ∧ ∀ u ∈ B, h (H u) = u
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5, first two bullets, of the supplied proof of cmcdt_lpi_lipschitz_piece_im (N_l = H(A_l) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin; a left inverse h_l of H on A_l is Borel on N_l), made global by extending h by a constant.

1. (Lusin–Souslin.) ℝⁿ is a Polish space and ℝ^P carries its Borel σ-algebra. If E ⊆ ℝⁿ is Borel, then H is continuous and injective on the Borel set B ∩ E, so H(B ∩ E) is Borel (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). With E := ℝⁿ, H(B) is Borel.
2. (Definition of h.) For y ∈ H(B) let h(y) be the unique u ∈ B with H(u) = y (unique because H is injective on B); for y ∉ H(B) put h(y) := 0. Then h(H(u)) = u for every u ∈ B.
3. (h is Borel.) Let E ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel. For y = H(u) ∈ H(B) with u ∈ B we have h(y) = u, so h(y) ∈ E iff u ∈ E; hence h⁻¹(E) ∩ H(B) = H(B ∩ E). Moreover h⁻¹(E) ∖ H(B) equals ℝ^P ∖ H(B) if 0 ∈ E and ∅ otherwise. Both pieces are Borel by step 1, so h⁻¹(E) is Borel, i.e. h is measurable.
(Equivalent Mathlib route: the restriction B.domRestrict H : B → ℝ^P is a measurable embedding (ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding), and h := Function.extend (B.domRestrict H) Subtype.val (fun _ => 0) is measurable by MeasurableEmbedding.measurable_extend and satisfies h(H(u)) = u for u ∈ B by Function.Injective.extend_apply.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Lusin–Souslin: H(B ∩ E) is Borel for every Borel E, since H is continuous and injective on the Borel set B ∩ E.
h := (H|_B)⁻¹ on H(B), extended by 0, satisfies h ∘ H = id on B.
h⁻¹(E) = H(B ∩ E) ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ H(B) if 0 ∈ E), which is Borel; so h is Borel.

subproblems.title: Integer density g∘H⁻¹ of a Lipschitz image piece and its area-formula bound (supplied steps 4–5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0, let H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz, and let B ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel such that H is injective on B and differentiable with injective derivative DH(a) = fderiv ℝ H a at every a ∈ B. Let g : ℝⁿ → ℤ be measurable and Lebesgue integrable on B, with g(u) ≠ 0 for every u ∈ B. Then there is a measurable m : ℝ^P → ℝ with m(y) ∈ ℤ for every y and m(H(u)) = g(u) for every u ∈ B, such that Hⁿ(H(B)) < ∞ and ∫⁻_{H(B)} |m| dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ·∫⁻_B |g| dλ in [0, ∞], where Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P and λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (H : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (g : Euclid n → ℤ), LipschitzWith L H → MeasurableSet B → InjOn H B → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ H a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ H a)) → Measurable g → IntegrableOn (fun u => (g u : ℝ)) B → (∀ u ∈ B, g u ≠ 0) → ∃ m : Euclid P → ℝ, Measurable m ∧ (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, m y = z) ∧ (∀ u ∈ B, m (H u) = g u) ∧ μHE[n] (H '' B) ≠ ∞ ∧ ∫⁻ y in H '' B, ‖m y‖ₑ ∂μHE[n] ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * ∫⁻ u in B, ‖(g u : ℝ)‖ₑ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the supplied proof of cmcdt_lpi_lipschitz_piece_im (the density m_l := g∘h_l on N_l = H(A_l) and 0 elsewhere; Hⁿ(N_l) < ∞ and ∫_{N_l}|m_l| dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫_{A_l}|g| dλ by the area formula), with the Jacobian bound J ≤ Lⁿ of its step 4.

Notation: DH(u) := fderiv ℝ H u, e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a ∈ Fin n), v(u) := (DH(u)e_a)_a, J(u) := √det(⟨DH(u)e_a, DH(u)e_b⟩)_{a,b}, N := H(B).

1. (Inverse.) H is Lipschitz, hence continuous on B, and injective on B. The sibling cmcdt_lpi_pc_measurable_inverse gives that N is Borel and a Borel map h : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ with h(H(u)) = u for every u ∈ B.
2. (Density.) Put m(y) := g(h(y)) (as a real number) for y ∈ N and m(y) := 0 for y ∉ N, i.e. m is the indicator of N times g∘h. Then m is measurable (N is Borel, g∘h is measurable and the cast ℤ → ℝ is measurable), m(y) is an integer for every y, and for u ∈ B we have H(u) ∈ N and m(H(u)) = g(h(H(u))) = g(u).
3. (Jacobian bound.) Let u ∈ B. Since DH(u) is injective, v(u) is linearly independent (the image of the basis (e_a) under a linear map with zero kernel). Part (ii) of the inherited prerequisite cmcdt_lpi_unit_orientation_span (the selected node's resolved dependency span_orientation, available as Submission.cmcdt_lpi_unit_orientation_span), applied to v(u), gives J(u) ≤ ∏_a |DH(u)e_a|. As H is L-Lipschitz, ‖DH(u)‖ ≤ L (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz), so |DH(u)e_a| ≤ ‖DH(u)‖·|e_a| = ‖DH(u)‖ ≤ L for each a, and J(u) ≤ Lⁿ.
4. (Area formula.) Apply part (ii) of the inherited prerequisite codim1_lura_gram_area_formula (the selected node's resolved dependency area_lintegral, the injective area formula with the Gram Jacobian in lintegral form) with m := n, f := H and s := B (B is Borel; H is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B and injective on B) to the weight y ↦ |m(y)| ∈ [0, ∞]: ∫⁻_N |m| dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(J(u))·|m(H(u))| dλ(u) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(J(u))·|g(u)| dλ(u), by step 2 on B. By step 3, ofReal(J(u)) ≤ ofReal(Lⁿ) = Lⁿ on B, so the last integral is ≤ ∫⁻_B Lⁿ·|g(u)| dλ(u) = Lⁿ·∫⁻_B |g| dλ.
5. (Finite measure.) The same area formula with the weight 1 gives Hⁿ(N) = ∫⁻_N 1 dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(J(u)) dλ(u) ≤ Lⁿ·λ(B), by step 3. Since g(u) is a nonzero integer for u ∈ B, |g(u)| ≥ 1 on B, so λ(B) ≤ ∫⁻_B |g| dλ < ∞ (g is integrable on B). Hence Hⁿ(N) < ∞. (Equivalently, |m| ≥ 1 on N gives Hⁿ(N) ≤ ∫⁻_N |m| dHⁿ.) Steps 2, 4 and 5 give all the claims. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lusin–Souslin (sibling measurable_inverse): N = H(B) is Borel and h ∘ H = id on B for a Borel h.
m := 1_N·(g∘h) is measurable and integer-valued with m(H(u)) = g(u) on B.
Hadamard's bound from span_orientation and ‖DH‖ ≤ L give J ≤ Lⁿ on B.
The Gram area formula gives ∫_N |m| dHⁿ = ∫_B J|g| dλ ≤ Lⁿ∫_B |g| dλ and Hⁿ(N) = ∫_B J dλ ≤ Lⁿλ(B) ≤ Lⁿ∫_B|g| dλ < ∞ (|g| ≥ 1 on B).

subproblems.title: Induced orientation J⁻¹·(α ↦ α(DH e)) of a bi-Lipschitz image piece: strongly measurable, a unit orientation of range DH, and of the approximate tangent plane Hⁿ-a.e. (supplied steps 4–5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0, κ > 0, let H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz, and let B ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel with κ·|a − a'| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| for all a, a' ∈ B, such that H is differentiable with injective derivative DH(a) = fderiv ℝ H a at every a ∈ B. Write e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1, v(u) := (DH(u)e_a)_{a ∈ Fin n} and J(u) := √det(⟨DH(u)e_a, DH(u)e_b⟩)_{a,b}. Then there is a strongly measurable η : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) such that (i) for every u ∈ B, η(H(u)) is a unit orientation of the subspace range DH(u) (IsUnitOrientationOf) and J(u)·η(H(u))(α) = α(v(u)) for every n-covector α on ℝ^P; and (ii) for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ H(B) (Hⁿ := μHE[n]) there is a linear subspace Q of ℝ^P with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (H(B)) y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (η(y)) Q.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (κ : ℝ) (H : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)), LipschitzWith L H → MeasurableSet B → 0 < κ → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, κ * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖H a - H a'‖) → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ H a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ H a)) → ∃ η : Euclid P → MultiVector P n, StronglyMeasurable η ∧ (∀ u ∈ B, IsUnitOrientationOf (η (H u)) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ H u : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)) ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ H u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1)) (fderiv ℝ H u (EuclideanSpace.single b 1)))) * η (H u) α = α (fun a => fderiv ℝ H u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))) ∧ ∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n].restrict (H '' B)), ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (H '' B) y Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (η y) Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4 and 5 (definition of η_l and the orientation bullet) of the supplied proof of cmcdt_lpi_lipschitz_piece_im; this is Simon's induced orientation, Ch. 6, 3.5 and 3.7 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 805–830): ξ_u := J(u)⁻¹·(α ↦ α(v(u))) orients range DH(u), η := ξ∘H⁻¹ on N := H(B), and N has approximate tangent plane range DH(u) at H(u) for a.e. u.

Notation: ev_z := (α ↦ α(z)) = ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ z ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) for z ∈ (ℝ^P)ⁿ; e'_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin P); λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ; N := H(B).

1. (Injectivity and inverse.) H is injective on B: if H(a) = H(a') with a, a' ∈ B, then κ|a − a'| ≤ 0, so a = a'. H is continuous, so the sibling cmcdt_lpi_pc_measurable_inverse gives that N is Borel and a Borel map h : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ with h(H(u)) = u for every u ∈ B.
2. (Definition.) For u ∈ ℝⁿ put ξ(u) := J(u)⁻¹·ev_{v(u)}, and put η(y) := ξ(h(y)) for y ∈ N and η(y) := 0 for y ∉ N (the indicator of N times ξ∘h). For u ∈ B, H(u) ∈ N and η(H(u)) = ξ(u).
3. (Strong measurability.) J is Borel (part (i) of the inherited prerequisite codim1_lura_gram_area_formula, the selected node's resolved dependency area_lintegral, with f := H), hence so is J⁻¹. For z ∈ (ℝ^P)ⁿ write z_{a,i} for the i-th coordinate of z_a, so z_a = Σ_i z_{a,i} e'_i; multilinearity gives ev_z = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (∏_a z_{a,f(a)})·ev_{(e'_{f(0)}, …, e'_{f(n−1)})}, a finite sum of fixed elements of Λ_n(ℝ^P) with real coefficients. With z := v(u), each coefficient u ↦ ∏_a (f(a)-th coordinate of DH(u)e_a) is Borel (measurable_fderiv_apply_const and continuity of coordinates). So u ↦ ev_{v(u)} is a finite sum of (Borel real function)·(constant vector), hence strongly measurable, and so is ξ = J⁻¹·ev_v. (No second-countability instance for MultiVector P n is needed; Lean does not synthesize one.) Consequently ξ∘h is strongly measurable (h is Borel) and η, its product with the indicator of the Borel set N, is strongly measurable.
4. (Unit orientation on B; claim (i).) Let u ∈ B. Since DH(u) is injective, v(u) is linearly independent. The inherited prerequisite cmcdt_lpi_unit_orientation_span (the selected node's resolved dependency span_orientation), applied to v(u), gives det(⟨v_a(u), v_b(u)⟩) > 0, so J(u) > 0, and some ξ' ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) that is a unit orientation of span(range v(u)) with α(v(u)) = J(u)·ξ'(α) for every α. Then ξ(u)(α) = J(u)⁻¹·α(v(u)) = ξ'(α) for all α, so ξ(u) = ξ', and J(u)·ξ(u)(α) = α(v(u)). Moreover span(range v(u)) = DH(u)(span{e_a}) = DH(u)(ℝⁿ) = range DH(u) (Submodule.span_image; the e_a span ℝⁿ). Since η(H(u)) = ξ(u) (step 2), η(H(u)) is a unit orientation of range DH(u) and J(u)·η(H(u))(α) = α(v(u)) for every α. This proves (i).
5. (Tangent planes for a.e. u ∈ B.) The inherited prerequisite ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae (the selected node's resolved dependency piece_tangent; F := H, B, L, m := κ, whose hypotheses are exactly ours) gives, for λ-a.e. b ∈ B, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N (H(b)) (range DH(b)). Let G be the set of b with this property. The complement of G is null for λ restricted to B, so there is a Borel set E' containing ℝⁿ ∖ G with λ(E' ∩ B) = 0 (exists_measurable_superset_of_null and Measure.restrict_apply).
6. (The exceptional image is Hⁿ-null.) Part (ii) of codim1_lura_gram_area_formula with s := E' ∩ B (Borel; H is differentiable with injective derivative and injective there) and weight 1 gives Hⁿ(H(E' ∩ B)) = ∫⁻_{H(E'∩B)} 1 dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{E'∩B} ofReal(J) dλ = 0, because λ(E' ∩ B) = 0.
7. (Claim (ii).) Let y ∈ N ∖ H(E' ∩ B). Then y = H(u) with u ∈ B ∖ E', so u ∈ G: N has approximate tangent space Q := range DH(u) at y, and η(y) = η(H(u)) is a unit orientation of Q by step 4. Hence every y ∈ N without such a Q lies in the Hⁿ-null set H(E' ∩ B), i.e. the property holds for Hⁿ⌞N-a.e. y (ae_restrict_iff', N being Borel). ∎
proof_key_steps: κ-co-Lipschitz gives injectivity on B; the sibling measurable_inverse gives N = H(B) Borel and a Borel left inverse h.
η := 1_N·(J⁻¹·ev_{v})∘h is strongly measurable via the finite coordinate expansion of ev_z, J being Borel.
span_orientation gives J > 0 and identifies J(u)⁻¹ev_{v(u)} with the unit orientation of span v(u) = range DH(u), so J·η(H u)(α) = α(v(u)).
piece_tangent gives the tangent plane range DH(u) at H(u) for a.e. u ∈ B; the area formula maps the exceptional λ-null set to an Hⁿ-null set, giving (ii).

subproblems.title: The Lipschitz image of an integer-weighted bi-Lipschitz piece is an integer multiplicity current with mass ≤ Lⁿ∫|g| (supplied steps 5–7; Simon 6.3.5–3.9)
subproblems.statement: Assume, as antecedents, (L3): for all N, k ∈ ℕ, every k-covector α on ℝ^N and every orthonormal family τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{k−1}) in ℝ^N, |α(τ)| ≤ |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm α); and (IMC)(b): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every IMRep R in U of dimension n and every E ⊆ ℝ^P, if U is open and E is Borel then there are a current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' representing A with R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R'.mult = R.mult and R'.orient = R.orient. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0, κ > 0, let H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz, and let B ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel with κ·|a − a'| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| for all a, a' ∈ B, such that H is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B. Let g : ℝⁿ → ℤ be measurable and Lebesgue integrable on B, with g(u) ≠ 0 for every u ∈ B. Then there is an integer multiplicity current Φ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) with M(Φ) ≤ Lⁿ·∫⁻_B |g| dλ and Φ(ω) = ∫_B g(u)·ω(H(u))(DH(u)e_0, …, DH(u)e_{n−1}) du for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), where DH(u) := fderiv ℝ H u and e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (N k : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid N) k) (τ : Fin k → Euclid N), Orthonormal ℝ τ → |α τ| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet E → ∃ (A : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents A ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (κ : ℝ) (H : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (g : Euclid n → ℤ), LipschitzWith L H → MeasurableSet B → 0 < κ → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, κ * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖H a - H a'‖) → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ H a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ H a)) → Measurable g → IntegrableOn (fun u => (g u : ℝ)) B → (∀ u ∈ B, g u ≠ 0) → ∃ Φ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity Φ ∧ Φ.mass ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * ∫⁻ u in B, ‖(g u : ℝ)‖ₑ ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, Φ ω = ∫ u in B, (g u : ℝ) * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (H u) (fun a => fderiv ℝ H u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 (the IMRep of one piece and (IMC)(b)), 6 (formula) and 7 (mass) of the supplied proof of cmcdt_lpi_lipschitz_piece_im, for a single piece B = A_l. This is Simon Ch. 6, 3.6–3.9 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 810–860) for an injective Lipschitz map on B: H_#(g[[B]]) = τ(H(B), |g∘H⁻¹|, ±induced orientation).

Notation: N := H(B); Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P; λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ; v(u) := (DH(u)e_a)_a; J(u) := √det(⟨DH(u)e_a, DH(u)e_b⟩)_{a,b}; Ψ_ω(u) := g(u)·ω(H(u))(v(u)).

1. (Injectivity; N Borel.) H is injective on B: H(a) = H(a') forces κ|a − a'| ≤ 0, so a = a' since κ > 0. H is continuous, so the sibling cmcdt_lpi_pc_measurable_inverse gives that N is Borel.
2. (Density and orientation.) The sibling cmcdt_lpi_pc_piece_multiplicity (H injective on B) gives a measurable, integer-valued m : ℝ^P → ℝ with m(H(u)) = g(u) for u ∈ B, Hⁿ(N) < ∞, and ∫⁻_N |m| dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ·∫⁻_B |g| dλ < ∞ (g is integrable on B). The sibling cmcdt_lpi_pc_piece_orientation gives a strongly measurable η : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) such that, for every u ∈ B, η(H(u)) is a unit orientation of range DH(u) and J(u)·η(H(u))(α) = α(v(u)) for every n-covector α, and such that for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (η(y)) Q.
3. (An IMRep.) Apply the inherited prerequisite cmcdt_ims_imrep_of_int_density (the selected node's resolved dependency int_density_imrep) with this P and n, U := ℝ^P (open), N, η and m. Its hypotheses hold: N is Borel and N ⊆ ℝ^P; N ⊆ range H with H Lipschitz, so N is countably n-rectifiable (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_range and CountablyRectifiable.mono); for every compact K, Hⁿ(N ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(N) < ∞ and ∫⁻_{N∩K} |m| dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_N |m| dHⁿ < ∞; η is strongly measurable; m is measurable and integer-valued; and the a.e. orientation condition is the last part of step 2. It gives an IMRep R in ℝ^P with R.action(ω) = ∫_N m(y)·η(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y) for every n-form ω.
4. (The current.) By the antecedent (IMC)(b) with U := ℝ^P (open), this R and E := ℝ^P (Borel), there are Φ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R' representing Φ with R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ ℝ^P = R.carrier, R'.mult = R.mult and R'.orient = R.orient. IMRep.action depends only on carrier, multiplicity and orientation, so R'.action = R.action. Hence Φ is integer multiplicity, and Φ(ω) = R'.action(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_N m·η(ω) dHⁿ for every test form ω.
5. (Formula.) Let ω be a test form. The inherited prerequisite codim1_lur_cd_injective_area_formula_gram (the selected node's resolved dependency area_integral, the injective area formula with the Gram Jacobian in Bochner form; G := H, F := B Borel, H differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B and injective on B), applied to h(y) := m(y)·η(y)(ω(y)), gives ∫_N m·η(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_B J(u)·m(H(u))·η(H(u))(ω(H(u))) du. For u ∈ B, m(H(u)) = g(u) and J(u)·η(H(u))(ω(H(u))) = ω(H(u))(v(u)) by step 2, so the integrand equals Ψ_ω(u) on B (setIntegral_congr_fun). Hence Φ(ω) = ∫_B Ψ_ω dλ, the asserted formula.
6. (Mass.) Φ.mass = Φ.massOn ℝ^P is the supremum of ofReal(Φ(ω)) over the test forms ω with |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for every y (massAdmissibleOn). Fix such ω. For y ∈ N, y = H(u) with u ∈ B, so η(y) is a unit orientation of some subspace: η(y)(β) = β(τ) for all β or η(y)(β) = −β(τ) for all β, with τ orthonormal. By the antecedent (L3), |η(y)(ω(y))| = |ω(y)(τ)| ≤ |ω(y)| ≤ 1. Hence ofReal(Φ(ω)) ≤ ‖∫_N m·η(ω) dHⁿ‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_N |m|·|η(ω)| dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_N |m| dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ·∫⁻_B |g| dλ (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, the pointwise bound on N, and step 2). Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M(Φ) ≤ Lⁿ·∫⁻_B |g| dλ. ∎
proof_key_steps: The siblings measurable_inverse, piece_multiplicity and piece_orientation give N = H(B) Borel, an integer density m = g∘H⁻¹ with ∫_N|m| dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫_B|g|, and an Hⁿ-a.e. orienting η with J·η(H u)(α) = α(DH(u)e).
cmcdt_ims_imrep_of_int_density (N is rectifiable as a subset of range H) gives an IMRep R with action ∫_N m η(ω); the antecedent (IMC)(b) with E = ℝ^P turns it into an integer multiplicity current Φ.
The Gram area formula gives Φ(ω) = ∫_B J·g·η(H)(ω(H)) dλ = ∫_B g·ω(H)(DH e) dλ.
For admissible ω, (L3) and the unit orientation give |η(ω)| ≤ 1 on N, so M(Φ) ≤ ∫_N|m| dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫_B|g| dλ.
